newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends sharply lower on Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends sharply lower on Deng's death.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed sharply lower against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday due to a resurgence of greenback-buying sparked by the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.625 against Wednesday's T$27.583 close. Turnover was a heavy US$393 million.
Dealers said profit-taking off a high U.S. dollar by foreign banks prevented further falls by the local currency.

"Although U.S. dollar demand increased with Deng's death, it was not enough to cause panic selling (of the Taiwan dollar), and the U.S. dollar maintained only a steady gain," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

Other dealers said the central bank may have intervened to bring the local currency up to as high as T$27.585 at one point. "The central bank also doesn't want to see wild rate swings," said another dealer.
